description: C4 suite release manifest — maps suite versions to component versions

1.0.18.notes: Verification patch; IDs are unchanged. Eight defects where c4 trusted metadata or stored names instead of rechecking bytes, found while dogfooding c4 to sync live state between two machines. (1) c4 diff <c4m> <dir> trusted size+mtime, so a corrupted copy that kept both reported no differences; the directory side is now always hashed. (2) Scans now settle racy files (git's racy rule), so a same-size rewrite within the second a scan saw a file is never recorded with stale content. (3) c4 patch hashes content as it copies from the store or a --source directory and refuses bytes that do not match their ID, leaving the destination untouched; it now exits 1 when any operation fails. (4) c4 cat verifies an object before printing it. (5) Stores written on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS) are readable on Linux. (6) c4 patch restores nested directory times, so c4 id after a sync matches the target. (7) c4 diff | c4 paths lists changed paths. (8) Malformed c4m exits 1 instead of panicking. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep from their 1.0.17 code.

1.0.17.notes: Correctness and safety patch; IDs are unchanged. (1) c4 id -s re-serialized any file whose content parsed as c4m, so the store held different bytes than the disk and the original was unrecoverable (#43); files are now stored exactly as read and c4 cat returns stored bytes verbatim. Trees containing c4m files snapshotted with <= 1.0.16 should be re-snapshotted. (2) c4 patch <c4m> <dir> followed symbolic links already in the destination and could write outside it; every write is now confined to the destination and refused through a link. (3) Scanning a symlink cycle (up -> ..) crashed with a stack overflow; the link now gets a null ID. (4) -S snapshots now store the folded ID-list object (#45); patch still cannot expand folded entries and refuses them as in 1.0.16 instead of writing the ID list as a file. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep from their 1.0.16 code.

1.0.16.notes: Correctness patch: three defects found by adversarial review of the shipped binary. (1) Durability ordering — batch-mode store objects were renamed to their final hash names before the end-of-command device barrier, so a power cut could leave a torn object at a valid name that a later run's write-skip would adopt silently; objects now publish only after the barrier, so presence at a hash name always implies bytes on stable media. (2) c4 log resolved the whole patch chain from scratch per section (super-quadratic; 1000 sections did not finish) — now resolves incrementally (1000 sections ~5s). (3) With sequence folding (-S), stored snapshots silently contained none of their frames because folded pattern names are not files; folded entries now expand to their members at store time. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep.

1.0.15.notes: Same-day supersede of 1.0.14 (which shipped with a Windows defect: the batch durability barrier fsync'd directory handles, which Windows refuses — spurious 'Access is denied' warnings on every c4 id -s / c4 patch and four failing store tests; no data loss). The barrier now routes through a platform-conditional store.SyncDir (no-op on Windows, F_FULLFSYNC on darwin, directory fsync elsewhere), verified on real Windows hardware. Also restores Go 1.16 buildability (legacy build-tag pairs, 1.16-compatible test code). Otherwise identical to 1.0.14: guided-scan directory-ID corruption fix (regenerate c4m files made with c4 id --continue on ≤1.0.13), bottom-up dir IDs (O(2^depth) → O(N)), path-keyed diff, null-timestamp rendering, safety defaults (pre-state capture with verbatim revert, protected paths, self-capturing snapshots), and the batch-barrier durability default with no flags (ingest ~180s → ~4.3s, materialize ~171s → ~4.4s on a 20k-file tree).

1.0.14.notes: SUPERSEDED same-day by 1.0.15 (Windows batch-barrier fix). Correctness/safety/perf patch. CRITICAL: c4m files produced by guided scans (c4 id --continue) on ≤1.0.13 have wrong directory IDs (the empty-input ID was written for every directory entry) and should be regenerated; file IDs were unaffected. Directory C4 IDs are now computed bottom-up, which also fixes O(2^depth) deep-tree scans (~93s → ~0.007s at depth 20). c4m.Diff keys entries by full path. Null timestamps render as - in structure mode. Safety defaults: c4 patch reconcile forms capture the destination's pre-state durably before applying and print a verbatim revert command; protected-path support closes a data-loss hazard (an unguarded patch could delete .git); snapshots are self-capturing (c4 cat <id> reproduces the manifest from the store alone). Performance: snapshot ingest ~180s → ~4.3s and materialize ~171s → ~4.4s on a 20k-file/105MB tree via the batch durability barrier — now the only durability behavior; the --no-fsync/--durable flags are removed. c4 gc (never released) was withdrawn before shipping. Only c4 has substantive changes; other components ship version-lockstep.

1.0.13.notes: Scan performance: O(D × N) propagateMetadata replaced with single-pass depth-stack (5.14M-entry trees went from 16-20 min hang to 2m 24s). Plus six API additions in c4: c4m.PropagateMetadata exported, c4m.WriteCanonical, scan.WithProgress, scan.WithMaxConcurrency, scan.WithContext, scan.WithEntryStream; progressive scanner propagation wired.

1.0.12.notes: Version bump to 1.0.12 across all components.

1.0.11.notes: Version bump to 1.0.11 across all components.

1.0.10.notes: Version alignment across all components. c4ts and c4-swift brought to 1.0.10.

1.0.6.notes: Initial coordinated release. TypeScript and Swift implementations, c4sh UX improvements, scan-everything fix.

1.0.19.notes: Patch. c4m canonical order: digit runs compare as integers of any length, never through a 64-bit or double parse, so a tree whose names hold runs of 20 or more digits has one ID instead of one per run (c4 Go, c4ts, c4-swift fixed; c4py was already right); text segments compare whole, a1 < ab (libc4 fixed). Shared vectors c4m/testdata/natural_sort_vectors.json in every implementation. Names with runs of 18 digits or fewer sort exactly as before, so their IDs are unchanged. Also c4git: the smudge filter passed through only the first 256 bytes of a non-pointer blob (data loss on checkout), fixed. c4-containers: README names C4_S3_ENDPOINT; s3worker passes S3_ENDPOINT through. Other components ship version-lockstep.

1.0.20.notes: Patch. c4: `c4 <name>` runs `c4-<name>` from PATH when no file or directory of that name exists, and `c4 help` lists the installed tools; nothing that works on 1.0.19 changes meaning. The suite archives and the Homebrew formula now bring the farm tools from c4-operator v0.2.0: c4-farm (all platforms), c4-agent and c4-unit (c4-agent on macOS and Linux), taken from that release's own archives; `brew install mrjoshuak/tap/c4` installs c4, c4sh, c4git and, through the tap's c4-farm and c4-agent formulas, `c4 farm`. Other components ship version-lockstep. Formula revision 1 (2026-10-26): the farm tools come from c4-operator v0.2.1, whose `c4 farm up` works on a fresh machine; the suite archives on the c4toolkit release still carry v0.2.0's c4-farm, c4-agent and c4-unit until 1.0.21. Formula revision 2 (2026-10-26): the farm tools come from c4-operator v0.2.2, whose embedded HUD matches its server (on v0.2.1 every write from the browser was refused: the HUD predated the X-C4-HUD header the server requires on cookie-authorized writes); the suite archives still carry v0.2.0's tools until 1.0.21.

1.0.21.notes: Patch. c4's `explain patch` now reports the plan `patch` would make, from the same sources, so content a folder already holds under another name counts (before, it said Missing for a switch between two views of files the folder holds, which `c4 patch` itself performs); otherwise every component ships version-lockstep. The suite archives and the Homebrew formula bring the farm tools from c4-operator v0.2.2, whose embedded HUD matches its server (on v0.2.1 every write from the browser was refused: the HUD predated the X-C4-HUD header the server requires on cookie-authorized writes), whose `c4 farm up` keeps an existing farm and its ports, whose `c4 farm down` no longer deletes c4-local by default, and whose status and up name `c4 farm open --as ROLE`. This also retires the 1.0.20 revision 1 split, where the formula carried v0.2.1 but the archives still carried v0.2.0.

1.0.22.notes: Superseded the same day by 1.0.23: the c4 binary built from the v1.0.22 tag reports `c4 1.0.21` (version constant not bumped). Tagged everywhere and published to PyPI, npm and ghcr, but never released on c4toolkit or the tap. Patch. The patch rule is fixed in every implementation at once: a c4m patch that restates a directory line identically and then lists children under it deepens that directory (erratum 2026-07-31); through 1.0.21 every implementation applied it as a removal of the whole subtree. c4: `c4 diff`'s patch of a null-ID directory whose only change was in its children was applied by `c4 patch` as removal, silently (fix on master since July, backported with the shared deepen-vs-remove conformance vector); patch and diff compare timestamps at the format's one-second resolution; `c4 id -s` no longer warns "failed to store l: is a directory" on a tree with a symlink to a directory (the link carries the directory's C4 ID, whose record the directory's own entry stores). c4py: the same rule in apply_patch, and the decoder's private copy of the rule is gone (it delegates to apply_patch). c4ts: the same rule; removing a directory now removes its descendants too (they were left as orphan entries while the root ID still matched); pretty timestamps carry a numeric zone offset (`-0600`) instead of a guessed zone abbreviation: an abbreviation a V8 parser cannot read is a bug, and numeric offsets are valid RFC 3339 for every decoder in the suite. c4-swift: the same rule and the same descendant fix. libc4: the same rule in c4m_apply_patch. Every implementation carries the shared vector as a test, and the CI matrices now run on pull requests against the release lines (c4ts and c4-swift gained CI). c4sh, c4git and c4-containers ship version-lockstep. The farm tools stay at c4-operator v0.2.2.

1.0.24.notes: Patch. c4: `c4 patch` hashes every file in the destination for the plan (through 1.0.23 it trusted size and mtime against the target, so a byte change under the same size and mtime was reported Reconciled and left in place); `-c GUIDE.c4m` is the stated way to trust size and mtime. A directory whose contents a plan changes gets its recorded time set back after the change, so a nested change no longer leaves the directory's mtime at the write time. `c4 id -s` refuses without a content store instead of silently scanning without storing. `c4 id DIR` with an unreadable file declares it on stderr and exits 2 instead of 0. Other components ship version-lockstep. The farm tools stay at c4-operator v0.2.2.

1.0.25.notes: Patch. c4: `c4 patch -q` of a names-only pretty description no longer removes every real file (a pretty line with a null C4 ID read its alignment padding into the name); a pretty line with a null timestamp no longer reads its padding into a link target (`c4 id -e` on a tree holding an epoch-dated symlink wrote a file that read back with every such link pointing elsewhere, a different ID, exit 0); `c4 cat -r` names every listing the store lacks and exits 2, and `c4 patch -r` refuses a partial tree; `c4 id -q` without `-s` says on stderr that it printed nothing. c4py: the same names-only deletion fix; a pretty time marked UTC was read as the reader's local time, hours wrong with no error and a different C4 ID, and is now read as UTC; numeric offsets (which c4ts writes) parse; an unknown zone abbreviation is still refused. c4ts: the same names-only deletion fix. The zero-versus-null rule stays out of every implementation on this line until core ships it: c4's 1.0.x pretty encoder writes ten dashes for a null mode, which a port with the rule would read as a known zero. c4-swift's v1.0.25 tag points at the commit v1.0.24 tags (524c392): c4-swift has no release line and no version site, and every commit on its main since 1.0.24 carries the zero-versus-null rule held out above, so the lockstep tag stays on the code that shipped. libc4, c4sh, c4git and c4-containers ship version-lockstep. The farm tools stay at c4-operator v0.2.2. Release record: the push CI run on c4 164fbd3 (run 42948145531) failed one leg, test (windows-latest, 1.21), on a timing flake in cmd/c4/internal/scan/progressive_scanner_test.go (a subtest that sleeps 50 ms and expects a non-empty snapshot); the pull-request run on the same commit had passed 7/7, nothing in 1.0.25 touches that scanner, and the failed leg passed on one re-run before the gate and the tag. The test is deflaked after the release.

1.0.26.notes: Proposed patch, awaiting Joshua's go; cut once each component's 1.0.26 commit has landed and passed the gate. Every implementation now reads a c4m line back as it was written, or refuses it naming the line: after a link operator one field is the C4 ID field and two are a target and the C4 ID field; pretty padding is never part of a name or target; a backslash always starts a two-byte escape, so a name or target ending in a backslash reads back as itself (c4 1.0.25's `c4 patch` silently left such files out of a materialised tree); a size token ends at a space and each mode position holds only its own letter or `-` (`6x real.txt` read as size 6 and the name `x real.txt`). Pinned by the shared link-target, backslash-name and damaged-line vectors in every implementation, except that Go's 1.0.x decoder loudly refuses 3 of the link-target vector's 10 shapes (null-mode links whose target starts with c4, written only by the library); the four ports read all 10, and Go reads them from 1.0.27. c4: the backslash and damaged-field rules; CI now runs the race detector (it never ran before). The race and test-deflake fixes touched cmd/c4/internal/scan, an internal package the CLI does not link, so they do not change c4 1.0.26's behaviour. c4 also: `c4 patch` no longer empties a directory the target lists only as one line; through 1.0.25 a one-level record (each subdirectory one line with its own C4 ID, as c4 1.1 stores a tree) removed every file under each such subdirectory with exit 0, and now a directory with no children listed is emptied only when its C4 ID is the empty listing's. c4 also: released 1.0.25 can delete a file whose name changes only in case, and can pair one file's name with another's bytes when two names fold together (case or Unicode form), silently, on default macOS and Windows disks. 1.0.26 measures each fold on the destination before writing, with no new dependency: the byte-order last name of a folded set is written whole, the others are refused and named with exit 2, a dry run writes nothing, and a file whose name changes only in case is kept and respelled. c4py: the decoder rules; and a directory's timestamp is its own mtime, as in Go and c4ts. c4py's scan C4 IDs change: through 1.0.25 c4py gave a directory its newest child's time and an empty directory the epoch, so its scan IDs differed from Go's on nearly every tree with a directory; they now match Go's (measured on real trees against the Go CLI). c4ts: the decoder rules; and released c4ts could delete a file whose only change was its modification time (reading a patch that restated it with a new time as a removal), and its own patches left such changes out; patches now use every-field identity, as the spec and Go do (pinned by the shared apply-from metadata-only case). c4-swift: the decoder rules, on a new release/1.0.x line from v1.0.25; a damaged mode is an error, no longer a null. Released c4m-swift refuses to read any c4m line whose name isn't ASCII, and keys names as Swift Strings, which treat the NFC and NFD spellings as one name, and its set operations compare entries by bare name, so same-named files in different folders were confused; 1.0.26 reads every name by its UTF-8 bytes and keys every name and path by them (the shared unicode-name vector). libc4: the decoder rules; released libc4 1.0.x silently read null-timestamp pretty lines with the padding inside names and targets, and 1.0.26 refuses every padded line, naming it; its encoder applied SafeName twice, so a name holding a backslash was written as a different name with a wrong root ID; an empty manifest's C4 ID is the ID of zero bytes, not nil (the shared empty-tree vector); its patch-chain reader shares the one line parser. Not included: c4ts main's unreadable-file scan change (a null C4 ID and a report instead of an abort), left for Joshua to decide with core's held #76; the collapsed-directory size fix (every implementation hashed a childless directory known only by its C4 ID with size 0; library reach only, planned for 1.0.27); and the zero-versus-null rule, which stays out of every implementation on this line until core ships it. c4sh, c4git and c4-containers ship version-lockstep. The farm tools stay at c4-operator v0.2.2.
